stem: A 10-week-old infant has returned to baseline after a BRUE; which historical feature should most raise concern for non-accidental injury during assessment?

options.text: The parents sought medical review immediately after the event
The caregiver reports the infant has fed normally since the episode
The caregiver gives changing versions of what happened
The infant was born at 39 weeks' gestation

explanation: Changing versions of what happened are concerning for non-accidental injury. In a BRUE assessment, inconsistent caregiver accounts are a red flag for possible abuse and should prompt further evaluation.

citations.source: Louisa Leone MD3 2025 - Child and Adolescent Health - Study Notes.pdf
citations.title: Louisa Leone MD3 2025 - Child and Adolescent Health - Study Notes

optionExplanations.A: Incorrect because immediate medical review is not a red flag for non-accidental injury; delay in seeking care is more concerning.
optionExplanations.B: Incorrect because normal feeding after the episode is not a warning sign for non-accidental injury.
optionExplanations.C: Correct because changing accounts of the event suggest an inconsistent history, which raises concern for non-accidental injury.
optionExplanations.D: Incorrect because being born at 39 weeks' gestation is not itself a red flag for non-accidental injury.
optionExplanations.E: Incorrect because a recent formula change is not a feature that increases concern for non-accidental injury in this setting.

sourceRefs: Louisa Leone MD3 2025 - Child and Adolescent Health - Study Notes.pdf
